en: I was looking for my beloved's grave,
I could not find it!.. It had been lost!..
With my heart choked with sobs I lamented:
“Where are you, my Suliko?!”
Among the thorns I noticed a rose
That had grown up there all alone,
With a fluttering heart I asked:
“Are you not Suliko?!”
As a sign of assent the bud
Stirred... it bowed its head,
Heavenly dew-pearls
It scattered down as tears.
Holding its breath, a nightingale
Had hidden among the leaves,
I spoke sweetly to the little bird:
“Are you not Suliko?!”
The singer fluttered its wings,
Touched the flower with its beak,
It sighed and twittered,
As if it said: “Yes, yes!”
A star was shining white upon us,
Its rays had come down,
I asked it in a rush:
“Are you not Suliko?!”
It gave me its assent by twinkling,
It poured its rays down on me,
And at that moment, whispering in my ear,
The breeze too brought me this good news:
“That is the one you were looking for,
Have done, and rest!
Bring your day to evening sweetly now
And bring your night to dawn!
“That one has been made into three:
A star, a nightingale, a rose,
Since you each other
Came to love in this world.”
I understood the sign!.. No longer do I seek
My beloved's coffin and grave,
No longer do I complain to the world,
No longer do I shed scalding tears!
I listen to the nightingale, I breathe in the rose,
I gaze at the star with joy,
And what I feel at that time
I cannot put into words with my tongue!
Life opened up for me again,
Which until this day had been bitterly cursed,
And now I know where you are:
You have your dwelling in three places, Suliko!
rom: Da, rasatsa vgrdznob me im dros,
notes: Romanization: the Georgian script has no capitals; the first word of a line and the name Sulik'o are capitalized here.
Suliko is a name of endearment, from 'suli', soul.
line 5.1: 'მგოსანი' is a poet or singer, here the nightingale.
line 5.3: 'ჩაიკვნესა' is to moan or sigh softly; 'ჩაიჭიკჭიკა' to twitter.
line 6.1: 'დაგვქათქათებდა' is 'was gleaming white upon us'.
line 6.3: 'შეფრქვევით' [?], literally 'with a sprinkling, a gush'; read here as 'in a rush (of feeling)'.
lines 8.2, 8.4, 9.2, 9.4: the ending -o marks reported speech (the breeze's words).
line 8.3-8.4: 'spend the day into evening ... spend the night until dawn', i.e. live your days and nights in peace.
